title: Use the scope attribute correctly
summary: A table uses the scope attribute wrongly. Use scope only on th cells, with the value col, row, colgroup or rowgroup.
problem: The scope attribute is used in a way HTML does not allow, for example with an invalid value or on a <td> cell. The attribute is meant for <th> header cells and takes col, row, colgroup or rowgroup.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users depend on header cells to know which row and column a data cell belongs to. A misused scope can make the table less clear for them, or be ignored.
steps: Find the cells with a scope attribute in the table reported by the scan.
Make sure scope is only on <th> elements. If it is on a <td> that works as a header, change the <td> to a <th>.
Use scope="col" for headers across the top and scope="row" for headers down the side.
Remove scope from simple tables where it adds nothing, and use headers and id on complex tables.
whyItMatters: This is a best practice, not a WCAG failure. Correct header markup is what lets assistive technology connect data cells to their headers, and invalid attributes make the table harder to maintain.
howToCheck: Inspect the table in your browser's element inspector. Every scope attribute should be on a th element and have the value col, row, colgroup or rowgroup.
